title: Morphisms out of the sheaf associated to a module
statement:
Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism], $R=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$, and for an $R$-module $M$ let $\mathcal F_M$, $c_M:M\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal F_M)$ and, for $R$-linear $u$, $\mathcal F_u$ be the associated $\mathcal O_X$-module, its canonical section map and the induced morphism [def-weil-pbc-associated-module]. For every sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules $\mathcal G$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], regard $\Gamma(X,\mathcal G)$ as an $R$-module. Then the map
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F_M,\mathcal G)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,\Gamma(X,\mathcal G)),\qquad\varphi\longmapsto\varphi_X\circ c_M$$
is bijective. It is natural in $\mathcal G$ and in $M$: for an $\mathcal O_X$-linear $\beta:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'$ it carries $\beta\circ\varphi$ to $\beta_X\circ(\varphi_X\circ c_M)$, and for an $R$-linear $u:M'\to M$ it carries $\varphi\circ\mathcal F_u$ to $(\varphi_X\circ c_M)\circ u$. (Stacks, Modules, Lemma 01BH, assertion (4), with $\alpha=\mathrm{id}_R$.)

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01BH (lemma-construct-quasi-coherent-sheaves), assertion (4), with alpha = id; proof there by adjointness of pi_* and pi^* (Sheaves, Lemma 0096) for pi : (X, O_X) -> ({*}, R) and the identification of constructions (1) and (3)

proof.text: *Reduction to presheaves.* Let $\mathcal G$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; it is in particular a presheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. By [def-weil-pbc-associated-module], $\mathcal F_M=\mathcal P_M^\#$ with the $\mathcal O_X$-linear sheafification map $\sigma_M:\mathcal P_M\to\mathcal F_M$, and by the universal property of sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] (on the site of opens of $X$, as in [def-weil-pbc-associated-module]) every $\mathcal O_X$-linear map $\psi:\mathcal P_M\to\mathcal G$ is $\varphi\circ\sigma_M$ for exactly one $\mathcal O_X$-linear $\varphi:\mathcal F_M\to\mathcal G$. Hence $\Sigma_{\mathcal G}:\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F_M,\mathcal G)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{PMod}(\mathcal O_X)}(\mathcal P_M,\mathcal G)$, $\varphi\mapsto\varphi\circ\sigma_M$, is bijective.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01BH (lemma-construct-quasi-coherent-sheaves), construction (3) and assertion (4), alpha = id; Sheaves, Lemma 0096 (lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules), proof, first equality (Hom out of the sheafified tensor presheaf)

proof.text: *From a presheaf map to a linear map.* For an $\mathcal O_X$-linear $\psi:\mathcal P_M\to\mathcal G$ put $E(\psi):M\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal G)$, $E(\psi)(m)=\psi_X(1\otimes m)$, where $\mathcal P_M(X)=\mathcal O_X(X)\otimes_RM=R\otimes_RM$. The map $m\mapsto1\otimes m$ is $R$-linear ($1\otimes rm=r\otimes m=r\cdot(1\otimes m)$ [def-weil-module-base-change]) and $\psi_X$ is $\mathcal O_X(X)=R$-linear, so $E(\psi)$ is $R$-linear for the $R$-module structure of $\Gamma(X,\mathcal G)=\mathcal G(X)$ as an $\mathcal O_X(X)$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. $E(\psi)$ determines $\psi$: for an open $U$, $a\in\mathcal O_X(U)$, $m\in M$, the restriction of $\mathcal P_M$ is $\rho^X_U\otimes\mathrm{id}_M$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-module], so $1\otimes m\in\mathcal P_M(U)$ is the restriction of $1\otimes m\in\mathcal P_M(X)$ ($\rho^X_U(1)=1$), and $a\otimes m=a\cdot(1\otimes m)$; since $\psi_U$ is $\mathcal O_X(U)$-linear and $\psi$ commutes with restrictions, $\psi_U(a\otimes m)=a\cdot\psi_U((1\otimes m)|_U)=a\cdot(\psi_X(1\otimes m))|_U=a\cdot E(\psi)(m)|_U$. The elements $a\otimes m$ generate $\mathcal P_M(U)$ as an abelian group and $\psi_U$ is additive, so $\psi$ is determined by $E(\psi)$: $E$ is injective.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 0096 (lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules), proof, second and third equalities (adjointness of tensor and restriction, then of restriction to f^{-1}O_Y and pushforward), specialized to pi : (X, O_X) -> ({*}, R), where f^{-1}O_Y is the constant ring R and the presheaf tensor product is P_M

proof.text: *From a linear map to a presheaf map.* Let $v:M\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal G)$ be $R$-linear. For an open $U$ the map $\mathcal O_X(U)\times M\to\mathcal G(U)$, $(a,m)\mapsto a\cdot v(m)|_U$, is additive in each variable and $R$-balanced: $R$ acts on $\mathcal O_X(U)$ through $\rho^X_U$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-module], and $a\cdot v(rm)|_U=a\cdot(r\,v(m))|_U=a\rho^X_U(r)\cdot v(m)|_U$ by the semilinearity of the restriction maps of $\mathcal G$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. By the universal property of $\mathcal O_X(U)\otimes_RM$ (the base change of $M$ to $\mathcal O_X(U)$ [def-weil-module-base-change]) it induces an additive $\psi^v_U:\mathcal P_M(U)\to\mathcal G(U)$ with $\psi^v_U(a\otimes m)=a\cdot v(m)|_U$. On generators, $\psi^v_U(b\cdot(a\otimes m))=\psi^v_U(ba\otimes m)=ba\cdot v(m)|_U=b\cdot\psi^v_U(a\otimes m)$ for $b\in\mathcal O_X(U)$, so $\psi^v_U$ is $\mathcal O_X(U)$-linear; and for $V\subseteq U$, $\psi^v_V((\rho^U_V\otimes\mathrm{id})(a\otimes m))=\rho^U_V(a)\cdot v(m)|_V=(a\cdot v(m)|_U)|_V$ (semilinearity and transitivity of restrictions in $\mathcal G$), so $\psi^v$ commutes with restrictions. Thus $\psi^v:\mathcal P_M\to\mathcal G$ is a morphism of presheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], and $E(\psi^v)(m)=\psi^v_X(1\otimes m)=1\cdot v(m)|_X=v(m)$. So $E$ is surjective, hence (Step 2) bijective with inverse $v\mapsto\psi^v$.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 0096 (lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules), proof, second and third equalities (adjointness of tensor and restriction, then of restriction to f^{-1}O_Y and pushforward), specialized to pi : (X, O_X) -> ({*}, R), where f^{-1}O_Y is the constant ring R and the presheaf tensor product is P_M

proof.text: *The composite is the stated map.* By Steps 1-3, $E\circ\Sigma_{\mathcal G}:\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F_M,\mathcal G)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,\Gamma(X,\mathcal G))$ is bijective, and $E(\varphi\circ\sigma_M)(m)=\varphi_X(\sigma_{M,X}(1\otimes m))=\varphi_X(c_M(m))$ by the definition $c_M(m)=\sigma_{M,X}(1\otimes m)$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-module]. So $\varphi\mapsto\varphi_X\circ c_M$ is bijective.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01BH (lemma-construct-quasi-coherent-sheaves), construction (3) and assertion (4), alpha = id; Sheaves, Lemma 0096 (lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules), proof, first equality (Hom out of the sheafified tensor presheaf)

proof.text: *Naturality.* For $\mathcal O_X$-linear $\beta:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'$: $(\beta\circ\varphi)_X\circ c_M=\beta_X\circ(\varphi_X\circ c_M)$, since components of a composite are composites of components [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For $R$-linear $u:M'\to M$ and $\varphi:\mathcal F_M\to\mathcal G$: $(\varphi\circ\mathcal F_u)_X\circ c_{M'}=\varphi_X\circ(\mathcal F_{u,X}\circ c_{M'})=\varphi_X\circ(c_M\circ u)=(\varphi_X\circ c_M)\circ u$, by $\mathcal F_{u,X}\circ c_{M'}=c_M\circ u$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-module].

split_report.summary: Read Stacks Modules 01BH (assertion (4), proof via pi^* -| pi_*) and Sheaves 0096 with its proof, and the definition def-weil-pbc-associated-module (F_M = sheafification of P_M: U -> O_X(U) (x)_R M, sigma_M, c_M, F_u). Statement kept. Wrote the proof in five steps that unwind the adjunction for pi : X -> point at the presheaf level: (1) Hom(F_M, G) = Hom of presheaves of modules (P_M, G) by the universal property of sheafification; (2) psi -> (m -> psi_X(1 (x) m)) is R-linear and injective (O_X(U)-linearity and compatibility with restrictions); (3) surjective, inverse v -> psi^v built from the universal property of the tensor product; (4) the composite is phi -> phi_X o c_M; (5) naturality in G and M (elementary, using F_{u,X} o c_{M'} = c_M o u from the definition). Only definitions are used (all Mathlib leaves or the definition node of this unit), no new nodes. stmt_deps kept. Added three Mathlib searches: Mathlib's SheafOfModules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction is a generalization only after the identification of F_M with an abstractly defined pullback to the point site, absent, so no match. The citer lem-weil-pbc-associated-module-pullback uses the bijection and its naturality in G (and injectivity), which the statement gives.
